thread:
Sam: Heads-up — after today's rate-limit rollout (rlimit-policy-2026-03-16) a handful of customers (notably acme-inc) are seeing repeated 429s. Not a full outage but spike in support tickets. Anyone on the canary side? link: https://grafana.redwood/team/rlimits/overview
Maria: I'm on it. Canary cluster-3 shows a sustained 12m spike starting at 10:12 UTC. P95 latency up ~60ms and request success drops. Logs have repeated: \"throttle: consecutive_tokens_exhausted\" for the same API keys.
Alex: That rollout lowered default-tier per-minute tokens from 600 -> 450 and adjusted burst window smoothing. Canary was 10% traffic. I deployed it at 09:52 UTC.
Priya: Customer sent this repro curl and error payload:
```\ncurl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" \
  -d '{\"prompt\":\"x\"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{\n  \"error\": \"Too many requests\",\n  \"code\": \"rate_limit.exhausted\",\n  \"retry_after\": 15\n}\n```
Sam: Important detail — their traffic is short, high-concurrency bursts (30–120 qps in <10s windows). Token-bucket smoothing might not be letting bursts through; the change reduced headroom.
Jordan: I pulled request traces for acme-inc: 95% of requests are small text completions, average tokens 18, but they do dozens of simultaneous connections from a single org key. Token refill math looks like it assumes more spread.
Maria: Can we reproduce locally? I ran a canary repro hitting cluster-3 with 120 concurrent short requests and got 30% 429s within 8s. Repro steps: 
1) use single API key
2) run 120 concurrent curl workers sending 50ms apart bursts for 20s
3) observe token bucket drain logs
I'll paste the script in the incident doc.
Alex: Thanks — that matches my simulation. The smoothing factor in the new policy reduces instantaneous burst allowance; intended to protect shared pools but seems aggressive for some customers.
OpsBot: Canary rollout rlimit-policy-2026-03-16 status: PARTIAL (10%) — paused autoscaling for cluster-3 at 10:25 UTC due to elevated 429 rate.
Priya: Support asks for mitigation we can tell acme-inc now — suggested: stagger client retries, add exponential backoff, or use a dedicated key for heavy burst traffic (we can offer temp Dedicated capacity).
Sam: Short-term plan: canary pause is fine. We need an engineering decision: tweak smoothing to restore some burst window for default tier or rollback to previous numeric limits. Which is quicker?
Alex: Quickest is rollback of rlimit-policy-2026-03-16 in canary and push previous policy (600/min with previous smoothing) to the canary subset. I'll prepare a rollback PR. Estimated 15–25 min to push + propagate.
Maria: Observability asks: add a dash tile showing consecutive_throttle_count and unique_keys_affected (per minute) — current dashboards don't surface consecutive throttle counts clearly. That's an action for eng-platform.
Jordan: Also recommend adding a synthetic test that runs the 120-concurrent burst against canary before rollout completion (preflight). Should be a gating step.
Priya: I'll reply to the customer with acknowledgement + mitigation tips and ETA for rollback. Offer to temporarily bump their quota if they need immediate relief (we can do that while rollback is in progress).
Sam: Alex — open rollback PR and ping us when merged. Maria/Jordan — capture repro script in the incident doc and add dashboard items. Priya — update customer message. I'll coordinate with SRE for monitoring during rollback.
Alex: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/rlimit-policies/pulls/422 — rollback to rlimit-policy-2026-03-01. Merging after +1.
Maria: Merged and applied to canary subset at 11:03 UTC. Metrics: consecutive_throttle_count dropped back to baseline within 90s, acme-inc 429 rate down to normal by 11:06 UTC.
OpsBot: Note: rollout pause cleared. Canary status: ROLLED_BACK -> STABLE.
Priya: Customer notified and replied that errors decreased and they can confirm their service is healthy. They asked what changed and if this will affect other customers. I told them we rolled back canary and we're iterating on smoothing before wider rollout.
Jordan: Follow-ups: (1) add preflight burst test to rollout pipeline, (2) create a short-runbook for support to quickly check consecutive_throttle_count and offer temporary quota bumps, (3) consider a staged smoothing delta so canary has intermediate headroom.
Sam: Good work. I'll create a ticket for the three follow-ups and assign to eng-platform and eng-sre. Closing thread once tickets are linked. :thumbsup:
